subject: maths
title: Shapes and Composite Objects: Name, Combine and Count Shapes and Objects
seo_title: Year 4 Composite Shapes and Objects Worksheets: 2-D Shapes, Composite Shapes and 3-D Objects (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Represent and approximate composite shapes and objects in the environment, using combinations of familiar shapes and objects
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on shapes and composite objects: name triangles, quadrilaterals, trapeziums, pentagons, hexagons and octagons, find the shapes that make a composite shape, count the shapes in a picture, and model a silo as a cylinder and a cone. 100 questions with an answer key, following the Australian Curriculum.
key_big: Big shapes and objects are made of smaller familiar ones: a house is a square and a triangle; a silo is a cylinder and a cone.
key_sub: Name a shape by counting its sides round the outside. A square is a special rectangle. When you count shapes or cubes, look for the big ones and the hidden ones too.
body_html:
Familiar 2-D shapes

A 2-D shape is flat. Name a shape by counting its sides. It has the same number of corners. A shape keeps its name when it is turned, and its sides do not have to be equal.

ShapeSides and cornersLook forIn real life
Triangle33 straight sidesa give way sign
Square44 equal sides, 4 right anglesa window pane
Rectangle44 right anglesa netball court
Trapezium4only 1 pair of parallel sidesa bucket seen from the side
Pentagon55 straight sidesthe outline of a house
Hexagon66 straight sidesa honeycomb cell
Octagon88 straight sidesa stop sign

A square has 4 right angles, so a square is a special rectangle.

Composite shapes

A composite shape is made of smaller familiar shapes. Look for the lines inside to find the parts. Then count the sides round the outside to name the whole outline.

Example 1

A house is a square with a triangle roof. How many sides does the whole outline have?

Go round the outside: 2 walls, the floor and 2 roof sides. The line between the roof and the walls is inside, so do not count it.

Answer: 5 sides, so the outline is a pentagon

Example 2

How many triangles are in this picture?

Count the small triangles: 2. Then look for bigger triangles made of smaller ones: the whole shape is 1 more. 2 + 1 = 3.

Answer: 3 triangles

Composite objects

Things around us are often made of familiar 3-D objects: cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones and spheres.

Real thingObjects that model it
Farm silo, rocket, crayoncylinder + cone
Ice-creamcone + sphere
House with a sloping roofrectangular prism + triangular prism
Tenttriangular prism
Shipping container, cereal boxrectangular prism
Example 3

How many cubes are in this solid stack?

Each layer has 2 × 2 = 4 cubes and there are 2 layers: 4 + 4 = 8. You can see only 7; 1 cube is hidden at the back.

Answer: 8 cubes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Saying a square is not a rectangleA square has 4 right angles, so it is a special rectangle
Adding the sides of the parts (4 + 3 = 7 for a house)Count only the sides round the outside
Forgetting the big shape made of small onesAfter the small shapes, look for shapes made of 2, 3 or more
Calling a tent a pyramidA pyramid comes to a point; a prism has the same shape at both ends
Counting only the cubes or faces you can seeRemember the ones at the back, underneath and inside
Using 2-D names for objects (a can is a “circle”)A can is a cylinder; only its ends are circles

faq.q: What is a composite shape in Year 4 maths?
faq.a: A composite shape is made of two or more familiar shapes, such as a house made of a square and a triangle. In the Australian Curriculum (AC9M4SP01), Year 4 students describe and draw composite shapes and objects using familiar shapes.
Yes. A rectangle is any 4-sided shape with 4 right angles, and a square has these too, so a square is a special rectangle with 4 equal sides.

faq.q: What is the difference between a shape and an object?
faq.a: A shape is flat (2-D), like a triangle or a circle. An object is solid (3-D), like a cone or a cylinder. A silo is an object made of a cylinder and a cone.

faq.q: How can my child practise composite shapes at home?
faq.a: Go on a shape hunt: find the shapes in road signs, buildings and playground equipment, and build houses, towers and rockets from blocks, boxes and tins. Then try the 100 questions on this page and check them with the answer key.

sets.title: Name 2-D shapes: sides, corners and right angles

items.q: What is the best name for this shape?
items.e: 4 equal sides and 4 right angles: a square. A cube is a 3-D object.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: The 2 corners on the left are right angles (square corners). The 2 corners on the right are not.

items.q: What is the best name for this shape?
items.e: 4 sides and 4 right angles, with 2 long and 2 short sides: a rectangle.

items.q: Which shape is a hexagon?
items.e: D has 6 sides, so it is a hexagon. A hexagon does not have to look like a honeycomb.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and 3 corners, so it is a triangle. A pyramid is a 3-D object.

items.q: Which shape is a quadrilateral?
items.e: A quadrilateral is any shape with 4 straight sides. A trapezium has 4 sides.

items.q: How many corners does a pentagon have?
items.e: A pentagon has 5 sides and 5 corners. Every shape with straight sides has as many corners as sides.

items.q: Which shape is a trapezium?
items.e: B is a trapezium: 4 sides and only 1 pair of parallel sides.

items.q: How many sides does an octagon have?
items.e: An octagon has 8 sides and 8 corners. Think of an octopus with 8 arms. A hexagon has 6.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: Count the sides: 6. A shape with 6 sides is a hexagon.

items.q: What is the name of this L shape?
items.e: Count the sides: 6. Any shape with 6 straight sides is a hexagon, even an L shape.

items.q: Is a square a rectangle?
c: Yes: it has 4 sides and 4 right angles.
No: a square has no right angles.
No: a rectangle must have 2 long and 2 short sides.
items.e: A rectangle has 4 sides and 4 right angles. A square has these too, so a square is a special rectangle with all sides equal.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: Count the sides: 5. A shape with 5 sides is a pentagon.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: 4 sides, and only the top and bottom sides are parallel (they go the same way): a trapezium.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: 5 corners are right angles. The inside corner of the L is bigger than a right angle (3 right angles), so do not count it.

items.q: Which shape has no straight sides and no corners?
items.e: A circle is one curved line. An octagon has 8 straight sides and 8 corners.

items.q: This shape looks like a house. What is its name?
items.e: Count the sides: 5. Any shape with 5 straight sides is a pentagon, even if the sides are not equal.

items.q: A shape has 6 straight sides. What is it?
items.e: 6 sides: a hexagon. 5 sides is a pentagon and 8 sides is an octagon.

items.q: What is the name of this shape?
items.e: Count the sides: 8. A shape with 8 sides is an octagon, like a stop sign.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: The 2 bottom corners are right angles, and so is the corner at the top. The other 2 corners are bigger than a right angle.

sets.title: Which shapes make this composite shape?

items.q: How many sides does the outline of the whole house have?
items.e: Go round the outside: 2 walls, the floor and 2 roof sides = 5 sides, so the outline is a pentagon. Do not add 4 + 3 = 7: the line where the roof meets the walls is inside.

items.q: Which shape is made from a square and a triangle?
items.e: A is a square with a triangle on top. The others are a rectangle and a triangle, a trapezium and a triangle, and 2 triangles.

items.q: Mei cuts a rectangle from one corner to the opposite corner. What two shapes does she get?
items.e: A cut from corner to corner makes 2 triangles. A cut across the middle would make 2 rectangles.

items.q: Which two shapes make this boat?
items.e: The sail is a triangle. The hull has 4 sides, with the top longer than the bottom: a trapezium.

items.q: Which shapes make this hexagon?
items.e: The line cuts the hexagon into 2 pieces. Each piece has 4 sides and 1 pair of parallel sides, so each is a trapezium.

items.q: This rectangle is made from squares of the same size. How many squares?
items.e: There are 2 rows of 4 squares: 4 + 4 = 8. Adding the rows and columns (4 + 2 = 6) does not count the squares.

items.q: You join 2 squares of the same size along one side. Which shape do you make?
items.e: 2 squares side by side make a rectangle twice as long as it is wide. It has 4 sides, not 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: Which shapes make this trapezium?
items.e: Count the pieces: 3 triangles. Pattern blocks work like this: 3 triangles make 1 trapezium.

items.q: How many triangles make this hexagon?
items.e: Count the triangles round the centre: 6. A hexagon has 6 sides, and each side belongs to one triangle.

items.q: Which shapes make this rectangle?
items.e: The line in the middle cuts the rectangle into 2 equal squares.

items.q: Which shapes make this square?
items.e: The line goes from one corner to the opposite corner. It cuts the square into 2 triangles.

items.q: A rectangle and a triangle make this shape. What is the name of the whole outline?
items.e: The sloping side of the triangle and the side of the rectangle go round the outside. The outline has 4 sides and 1 pair of parallel sides: a trapezium.

items.q: Which shapes make this L shape?
items.e: A tall rectangle and a flat rectangle make the L. Neither piece has 4 equal sides, so they are not squares.

items.q: Which two shapes make this tree?
items.e: The leaves are a triangle and the trunk is a thin rectangle.

items.q: Two right-angled triangles are the same. You join them along their longest sides. Which shape can you make?
items.e: Put the triangles together like the two halves of a sandwich cut corner to corner: they make a rectangle with 4 right angles.

items.q: Which shapes make this rocket?
items.e: The body is a rectangle. The nose is a triangle and there is a triangle fin on each side: 1 + 2 = 3 triangles.

items.q: Which two shapes make this big triangle?
items.e: The top piece is a small triangle. The bottom piece has 4 sides and 1 pair of parallel sides: a trapezium.

items.q: A rectangle and 2 triangles make this shape. What is the name of the whole outline?
items.e: Go round the outside and count the sides: 6. So the outline is a hexagon.

items.q: Which two shapes make this house?
items.e: The walls are a square (4 equal sides) and the roof is a triangle (3 sides).

items.q: Which two shapes make this arrow?
items.e: The long part is a rectangle and the point is a triangle.

sets.title: Count the shapes in a picture

items.q: What shape is the hull (the bottom part) of this boat?
items.e: The hull has 4 sides. The top and bottom are parallel but not the same length, so it is a trapezium.

items.q: How many circles are in this train?
items.e: 2 wheels on the carriage and 3 wheels on the engine: 2 + 3 = 5 circles.

items.q: How many triangles can you find in this picture?
items.e: There are 2 small triangles, and together they make 1 big triangle: 2 + 1 = 3.

items.q: How many shapes are in this robot altogether?
items.e: Count every shape: 3 triangles + 1 square + 6 rectangles + 4 circles = 14. Do not forget the eyes, mouth and buttons drawn on top of other shapes.

items.q: How many triangles can you find in this picture?
items.e: 4 small triangles, and the big triangle made of all 4: 4 + 1 = 5.

items.q: How many rectangles can you find? (A square is a rectangle too.)
items.e: 3 small ones, 2 made of 2 small ones next to each other, and 1 big one: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.

items.q: Ruby counts the triangles in this picture and gets 4. What did she forget?
c: the big triangle made by all 4
items.e: There are 4 small triangles, but all 4 together make 1 big triangle too. 4 + 1 = 5.

items.q: How many rectangles are in this robot? (A square is a rectangle too.)
items.e: Mouth, body, 2 arms and 2 legs are 6 rectangles. The square head is a rectangle too: 6 + 1 = 7.

items.q: How many squares can you find?
items.e: 4 small squares, and the big square around all of them: 4 + 1 = 5.

items.q: How many triangles are in this boat?
items.e: 2 sails and the little flag at the top of the mast: 2 + 1 = 3 triangles.

items.q: How many rectangles are in this train? (A square is a rectangle too.)
items.e: 4 rectangles (carriage, engine, chimney, the join between them) and 3 squares, which are rectangles too: 4 + 3 = 7.

items.q: How many triangles are in this robot?
items.e: 1 on top of the head and 1 ear on each side: 1 + 2 = 3 triangles.

items.q: How many rectangles are in this picture? (A square is a rectangle too.)
items.e: The door and the tree trunk are rectangles (2). The 3 squares are rectangles too: 2 + 3 = 5.

items.q: How many triangles can you find in this picture?
items.e: 3 small triangles, 2 triangles made of 2 small ones next to each other, and 1 big one: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.

items.q: How many squares are in this train?
items.e: 2 square windows on the carriage and the square cabin on the engine: 2 + 1 = 3 squares.

items.q: How many circles are in this robot?
items.e: 2 eyes and 2 buttons: 2 + 2 = 4 circles.

items.q: How many triangles can you find in this square?
items.e: 4 small triangles meet in the middle. Each diagonal also cuts the square into 2 big triangles: 2 + 2 = 4 more. 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: How many rectangles can you find? (A square is a rectangle too.)
items.e: There are 2 squares, and they make 1 big rectangle together: 2 + 1 = 3.

items.q: How many squares are in this picture?
items.e: The 2 windows are squares, and so are the walls of the house: 2 + 1 = 3 squares.

items.q: How many shapes are in this picture altogether?
items.e: 3 squares + 2 rectangles + 2 triangles + 1 circle = 8 shapes.

sets.title: 3-D objects in the world around us

items.q: This is a solid stack of cubes with no gaps. How many cubes are in it?
items.e: Each layer has 2 × 2 = 4 cubes and there are 2 layers: 4 + 4 = 8. You can see only 7 of them; the other 1 is hidden behind the others.

items.q: A water tower is a sphere on top of a tall cylinder. You draw it flat, as you see it from the front. Which 2-D shapes do you draw?
items.e: From the front, a sphere looks like a circle and a standing cylinder looks like a rectangle. Sphere and cylinder are the names of the 3-D objects, not the flat drawing.

items.q: This is a solid stack of cubes with no gaps. How many cubes are in it?
items.e: Each layer has 3 × 3 = 9 cubes and there are 2 layers: 9 + 9 = 18. You can see only 14 of them; the other 4 are hidden behind the others.

c: a square-based pyramid and a sphere
items.e: The scoop is round like a ball: a sphere. The cone comes to a point and has a circle at the top: a cone.

items.q: A round rainwater tank on a farm is closest to which object?
items.e: It has a circle at the top and bottom and a curved side: a cylinder.

items.q: A shipping container is closest to which object?
items.e: It has 6 rectangle faces and is longer than it is tall: a rectangular prism.

items.q: A roof made of 4 triangles that meet at a point on a square base is closest to which object?
items.e: A square base and 4 triangle faces that meet at a point: a square-based pyramid.

items.q: This tent is shaped like which object?
items.e: It has a triangle at each end joined by rectangles, and it does not come to a point: a triangular prism.

items.q: Amelia says a tent with a triangle at each end is a pyramid. Why is she wrong?
c: It does not come to a point, so it is a prism.
items.e: A pyramid comes to a point. A tent like this has the same triangle at both ends, so it is a triangular prism.

items.q: A basketball is closest to which object?
items.e: It is round all over: a sphere. A circle is a flat 2-D shape.

items.q: A traffic cone is closest to which object?
items.e: It has a circle base, a curved surface and a point: a cone. A pyramid has flat triangle faces.

items.q: This is a solid stack of cubes with no gaps. How many cubes are in it?
items.e: Each layer has 3 × 2 = 6 cubes and there are 2 layers: 6 + 6 = 12. You can see only 10 of them; the other 2 are hidden behind the others.

c: a triangular prism and a cone
items.e: The long part is a cylinder and the tip is a cone. A rectangle and a triangle are only the flat outline.

items.q: This model house is made of two objects. Which two?
c: a rectangular prism and a square-based pyramid
a rectangular prism and a triangular prism
items.e: The bottom has 6 rectangle faces: a rectangular prism. The roof has a triangle at each end and does not come to a point: a triangular prism.

items.q: Which of these is made of a cylinder with a cone on top?
items.e: A rocket has a cylinder body and a cone nose. A cricket ball is a sphere, a dice is a cube and a tissue box is a rectangular prism.

items.q: A dice is closest to which object?
items.e: It has 6 square faces of the same size: a cube.

items.q: How many faces does this tent have? Count the floor too.
items.e: You can see only 2 faces. A tent has 2 triangle ends and 3 rectangles (2 sloping sides and the floor): 2 + 3 = 5.

items.q: A long chocolate box with a triangle at each end is closest to which object?
items.e: 2 triangle ends joined by 3 rectangles: a triangular prism.

c: a cylinder and a square-based pyramid
items.e: The tall part has 2 circle ends and a curved side: a cylinder. The roof has a circle base and a point: a cone. Rectangles and triangles are flat 2-D shapes.

items.q: This tower is made of two objects. Which two?
c: a cube and a square-based pyramid
a cube and a triangular prism
items.e: The bottom has 6 square faces: a cube. The top has 4 triangle faces that meet at a point: a square-based pyramid. A cone has a circle base.

sets.title: Real-world problems: model things with shapes and objects

items.q: Sienna makes a hexagon from 6 triangles. Each side of a triangle is 5 cm. What is the distance around the hexagon?
items.e: Only the 6 sides on the outside count: 6 × 5 = 30 cm. The lines inside the hexagon are not part of the outline.

items.q: A give way sign in Australia is closest to which shape?
items.e: A give way sign has 3 sides (it points down), so it is a triangle.

items.q: Chloe glues one cube on top of another. How many square faces are on the outside now?
items.e: 2 cubes have 6 + 6 = 12 faces. The 2 faces glued together are hidden: 12 − 2 = 10.

items.q: A stop sign is closest to which shape?
items.e: A stop sign has 8 straight sides, so it is an octagon. Count carefully: 6 sides would be a hexagon.

items.q: Harper glues a square-based pyramid on top of a cube to make a tower. How many faces are on the outside of the tower?
items.e: Cube 6 + pyramid 5 = 11 faces, but the top of the cube and the bottom of the pyramid are glued together and hidden. 11 − 2 = 9.

items.q: A netball court is closest to which shape?
items.e: A netball court has 4 straight sides and 4 right angles, and it is longer than it is wide: a rectangle.

items.q: Liam puts 3 stop signs in a row for a road safety lesson. Each stop sign is an octagon. How many sides are there altogether?
items.e: An octagon has 8 sides. 3 octagons: 3 × 8 = 24 sides. 18 would be 3 hexagons.

items.q: Lachlan draws houses. Each house is a square with a triangle roof, a rectangle door and 2 square windows. He draws 3 houses. How many squares does he draw?
items.e: Each house has 1 square wall + 2 square windows = 3 squares. 3 houses: 3 × 3 = 9.

items.q: A tennis ball tube is closest to which object?
items.e: It has a circle at each end and a curved side: a cylinder.

items.q: 1 trapezium pattern block covers the same space as 3 triangle blocks. A hexagon is 6 triangle blocks. How many trapezium blocks cover a hexagon?
items.e: 6 triangles ÷ 3 triangles in each trapezium = 2 trapeziums. You can see this in a hexagon cut in half.

items.q: A silo is a cylinder with a cone roof. How many flat faces does the whole silo have?
items.e: A cylinder has 2 flat circle faces and a cone has 1. The cone sits on the top circle of the cylinder, so both of those are hidden. Only the circle on the ground is left: 1.

items.q: A lighthouse with a pointed roof can be modelled with which two objects?
c: a cylinder and a triangular prism
items.e: The tall round tower is a cylinder and the pointed roof with a circle base is a cone.

items.q: A slice cut from the centre of a round pizza is closest to which shape?
items.e: The slice has 2 straight sides that meet at a point in the middle and a slightly curved crust: close to a triangle.

items.q: Charlotte makes a model pine tree: a cone on top of a thin cylinder trunk. How many curved surfaces does the model have?
items.e: A cone has 1 curved surface and a cylinder has 1 curved surface: 1 + 1 = 2.

items.q: A bucket is wider at the top than at the bottom. From the side, it looks closest to which shape?
items.e: From the side you see 4 sides: the top and bottom are parallel but the top is longer. That is a trapezium.

items.q: A shoebox lid is lying flat on the table. Seen from above, it is closest to which shape?
items.e: From above you see only the flat top of the lid: 4 sides and 4 right angles, longer than it is wide. That is a rectangle.

items.q: Ava builds a solid block of cubes 4 long, 2 wide and 3 high. How many cubes does she use?
items.e: Each layer is 4 × 2 = 8 cubes. 3 layers: 8 + 8 + 8 = 24. From one corner you can see only 18; 6 are hidden behind the others. Adding 4 + 2 + 3 = 9 does not count the cubes.

items.q: Which object is closest to the shape of a cricket ball?
items.e: A cricket ball is round all over: a sphere.

items.q: The Australian 50c coin has 12 straight sides. How many corners does it have?
items.e: A shape with straight sides has the same number of corners as sides: 12 sides, 12 corners.

items.q: Isla uses triangle pattern blocks. 6 triangles make 1 hexagon. How many triangles does she need for 3 hexagons?
items.e: Each hexagon needs 6 triangles: 3 × 6 = 18.
